From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: VPC connectivity sales discovery  integration follow-up

Hi Alex / Priya,

Great to speak with you both this morning  thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery call and suggested next steps on the integration side:

Summary of ask:
- FinPay will host the Redwood inference calls from a private environment and requires private connectivity (VPC endpoints / IP allowlist) for all API traffic.
- Concerns: egress behavior, DNS resolution, mTLS termination, and embedding/reranker latency for low-latency queries.

What we covered / recommendations (high level):
- We support VPC endpoints and IP allowlist options. For lower latency and isolated traffic we recommend a private endpoint in the same region with an allowlist for FinPay NATs.
- DNS/egress: we can support private DNS resolvers or configure egress through a controlled proxy. If you need full egress lock-down, our Private deployment (VPC) is the pattern we typically use.
- mTLS: Redwood supports mTLS for mutual authentication on private endpoints  SE team can share sample cert exchange steps.
- Auth/SDK: use API keys scoped to the service account + short-lived tokens for server-to-server calls. Our SDK supports automatic retries and structured output/tool-calling patterns for rerankers and embeddings.

Attachments: I attached a short runbook and checklist with our recommended config and a sample integration diagram.

Proposed next step: Technical deep-dive with your infra and our SEs to walk through network requirements and sample configs. I broke out two options:
- Option A (recommended): 60-min deep-dive with Marissa + Jonas to review VPC endpoints, allowlist, DNS, and mTLS.
- Option B: if you prefer, we can do a short async Q&A first and follow with a targeted session.

Are you available for a technical session next week? I can do Wed 4/21 or Thu 4/22 morning PT.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Hi Alex  good questions, answered briefly below and SEs will bring the details to the deep-dive.

1) IP ranges/ports: We prefer IP allowlist entries limited to our private endpoint IP(s). For hosted customers we can provide a small set of stable egress IPs (typically a /32 or small set per region)  SE will confirm exact ranges for your region. Required ports: 443 (TLS) and 2197 (optional outbound for telemetry)  we'll confirm exact port list in the call.

2) DNS: Private endpoint uses cloud-provider private DNS when deployed in the same VPC/region. If you use allowlist-only egress from your environment to our hosted endpoint, you may need to forward DNS for api.redwood.com to the private IP; sample resolver configs are in the runbook.

3) mTLS: Optional but recommended for highest assurance. It's configurable per-route. For the deep-dive Jonas will share cert exchange steps and a sample nginx/Envoy config.

I've proposed Wed 2027-04-21 10:00 AM PT for the 60-min technical deep-dive. If that works I'll send the invite and include Marissa and Jonas.

Also included is a short checklist of what our infra team typically asks for ahead of the call (attached).

Thanks,
Lauren

Hi Alex / Priya  Jonas from Redwood SE team here. Quick tech notes to unblock your infra review prior to Wed's deep-dive. I'll walk through these live but wanted to put them in writing: 

VPC endpoints / networking patterns:
- Option 1 (recommended): Private endpoint in the same cloud region using provider-specific Private Service Connect (GCP) or PrivateLink (AWS). The endpoint exposes a private IP that you can add to your allowlist; traffic stays on the provider backbone.
- Option 2: Allowlist outbound to our regional egress IPs. This is simpler for immediate access but exposes across public network egress.

IP ranges & ports:
- We can provide 1-3 /32 addresses per region for private endpoints. For allowlist egress we provide a small set of stable IPs.
- Ports: 443 (required), 80 (redirects only), optional telemetry ports (2197) and SSH only for customer-managed deploys (on request).

DNS and Egress:
- If you use a private endpoint, our recommendation is to create a private DNS record (api-redwood.internal) pointing to the endpoint IP. If you can't modify DNS, you can add host entries or forward only the necessary domains to your resolver.
- Egress from your environment to our endpoint will not require NAT traversal if endpoints are peered in the same VPC. For cross-account setups we provide detailed peering guidance in the runbook.

mTLS & certs:
- mTLS is supported and can be enforced per-route. We support both client certs and OAuth2-based short-lived tokens. Typical setup: you provision a client cert, upload the CA fingerprint to our control plane, and we validate on socket connect. Sample Envoy config and cert rotation steps are in the attached runbook.

Embeddings / rerankers and routing:
- For low-latency embeddings/reranker calls we recommend colocating the request path in the same region and enabling prefix caching. We'll configure a model routing policy to route latency-sensitive calls to the low-latency pool.
- SDK notes: our SDK supports structured output and tool-calling; for reranker pipelines we recommend batched embedding uploads and streaming responses for ranking results.

What we need from FinPay ahead of the call:
- Network contact + preferred deep-dive time (confirm Wed 4/21 10:00 AM PT if possible).
- A list of IP ranges/NATs from your environment and whether you can create private DNS entries.
- Any compliance constraints on cert management or KMS requirements.

I'll bring sample configs and the VPC architecture diagram to the session.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
